title: An improved lower bound for the minimum-autocorrelation constant
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18888v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We construct nonnegative bounded compactly supported functions on the real line that give the lower bound $\mathcal{A}\ge 0.4103779774321214877852987\ldots$ for the minimum-autocorrelation constant. This improves the explicitly certified bound $2378625/5958277=0.39921356\ldots$ reported by Russell. The construction combines a point mass with a monotone degree-ten polynomial density; a one-sided atom-removal argument then produces ordinary functions. Its numerical content reduces to exact rational polynomial identities and 20 Bernstein subinterval certificates. The finite certificate, actual overlap integrals, admissibility, mass formula, and ordinary-function witness bounds have been formalized in Lean 4.19.0; the pinned proof sources and recorded audit are supplied. The passage to the supremum constant is given separately as a mathematical argument. As applications, the same construction yields an upper bound below $1.5610183$ for the large-multiplicity generalized-difference-basis coefficient and a feasible squared mass below $2.436778$ for a continuous sparse-ruler relaxation. An appendix quantifies the loss under independent sampling followed by completion. No improved bound for the complete sparse ruler constant, or global optimality of the construction, is asserted.

title: Harmonic numbers and Lerch functions behind falling factorial generating functions
authors: Hemen Dutta, Gradimir V. Milovanovic, Yilmaz Simsek
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18893v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study a family of special numbers and polynomials introduced by Simsek whose exponential generating function has as denominator a falling factorial in the exponential variable. Using the partial fraction decomposition of this denominator, each member of the family is expressed by a single finite sum involving Bernoulli polynomials, Apostol Bernoulli polynomials and two variable Fubini polynomials evaluated at reciprocals of integers. A second expansion, around the point where the denominator vanishes, expresses the same numbers through Stirling numbers of the second kind and generalized harmonic numbers, and yields closed formulas for the first few members. We construct a function, built from the Hurwitz zeta function and Lerch s transcendent, which interpolates the polynomials at the negative integers and gives a closed form of a multiple series recently introduced by Pokaz, Ribicic Penava and Simsek, we give an Euler type integral representation for it, and show that the numbers are signed combinations of moments of geometric random variables. Recurrence relations, asymptotics and an extension to arbitrary distinct nodes are also given.

title: On the nonnegative integer solutions to the equation $F_n^2+F_m=2^{a}$
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18894v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Diophantine equation $F_n^x+F_m^y=2^a,$ where $F_k$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number and $n,m,a\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$, has attracted attention in recent years. The cases $(x,y)=(1,1)$ and $(x,y)=(2,2)$ were completely resolved by Bravo and Luca, and by Jeong and Park, respectively. In this note, we investigate the mixed exponent case $(x,y)=(2,1)$ and we completely determine all nonnegative integer solutions.

title: A Symbolic Differentiation_Summation Framework for Power Sums of Arithmetic Sequences
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18898v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give a self-contained derivation of the closed form of the power sums $S_m(n)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(a_0+(i-1)d)^m$ in which the Bernoulli numbers enter as constants of integration rather than as prescribed coefficients. The derivation rests on an elementary fact: a sum whose terms are polynomial in the index is the restriction to the integers of a unique polynomial, which satisfies the defining difference equation identically and may therefore be differentiated and integrated exactly. Differentiating lowers the power by one; integrating back introduces a single constant, equal to the slope $S_m'(0)$ of the polynomial at the origin and fixed by the value $S_m(1)=a_0^m$. This yields a closed form for $S_m(n)$ in terms of the constants and a recurrence that determines them, obtained without induction on the exponent and without generating functions. With the Bernoulli numbers defined by their classical recurrence, we identify the constants as $d^mB_m(a_0/d)$; the progression starting at $0$ reproduces that recurrence exactly. In the normalized case they are $B_m(1)$, so $C_1=B_1(1)=+\tfrac12$, a value that reflects the summation range; a reflection identity shows, without generating functions, that the odd constants beyond the first vanish. The coefficients of the recurrence are scaled binomial coefficients from a single row of Pascal's triangle, and the same approach gives closed forms for sequences with polynomial differences. The integral recursion behind the method is known in the normalized case; each result is related to its classical counterpart, and a verified implementation is provided.

title: Adjoint Transfer and Order-Lifting Dichotomies for 2 x 2 Matrices over Prime-Power Rings
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18900v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For an odd prime p, we study the change in matrix order under lifting from Z/p^k Z to Z/p^(k+1) Z. The first variation of the order defect is an affine translate of a cyclic adjoint transfer on sl_2(F_p). We classify the full-order transfer for every q in GL_2(F_p): its rank is 3 for scalar elements, 1 for nonscalar semisimple elements, 1 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p = 3, and 0 for nonscalar Jordan elements when p > 3. For a Jordan element q = lambda(I + U), U^2 = 0 and U != 0, the vanishing first-order transfer for p > 3 admits an exact higher-order refinement. Writing d = (p - 1)/2, the full-order perturbation has depth d when tr(UX) != 0, depth p - 1 when tr(UX) = 0 and X is not in the span of U, and vanishes identically for X in the span of U. For p = 3, among the 27 lifts of a nonscalar order-preserving parent with determinant fixed to +1 or -1, exactly 9 preserve its order and 18 triple it; after the first increase, every further lift triples the order. We also give a scalar obstruction criterion for order preservation among unrestricted Jordan lifts.

title: The Diagonal of a Regular Pentagon
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We demonstrate the well-known fact that the diagonal of a unit regular pentagon has length the golden ratio. While similar to other proofs, we provide a novel figure that we believe is particularly well-suited to achieve full understanding at a glance.

title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18905v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.

title: Cyclic Kronecker Fourier Transforms, Weber Norms, and Rogers-Ramanujan Singular Values
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18910v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field with fundamental discriminant $D=-5n$, where $n>0$ is odd, and cyclic ideal class group $\text{Cl}(K)=\langle g\rangle\simeq C_{4M}$. Assume that the ramified prime class above $5$ is the unique involution $g^{2M}$. For the Kronecker eta invariant \[
  F(A)=\frac{|\eta(z_A)|^2}{\sqrt{a_A}}, \] where $z_A$ and $a_A$ arise from a positive definite quadratic form representing the ideal class $A$, we show that the logarithms of the mirror ratios \[
  R_j=\frac{F(g^{2M-j})}{F(g^j)},\qquad 0\le j<M, \] are related by an explicit discrete cosine transform to the odd class-character Hecke $L(1)$-values. A single level-$5$ generalized-Weber orbit realizes all of these mirrors. Combining Fourier nonvanishing, lower-power Weber class invariants and a ray-class cancellation argument, we prove \[
  \mathbb{Q}(R_j)=H^{\langle c\rangle},\qquad
  R_j^{\sigma^{2M}}=R_j^{-1},\qquad
  \mathbb{Q}(R_j+R_j^{-1})=H^{\langle c,\sigma^{2M}\rangle}. \] Here $H$ is the Hilbert class field, $c$ denotes complex conjugation, and $\sigma$ corresponds to $g$ under the Artin map. Consequently \[
  [\mathbb{Q}(R_j):\mathbb{Q}]=4M,\qquad
  [\mathbb{Q}(R_j+R_j^{-1}):\mathbb{Q}]=2M, \] and the latter degree becomes $M$ over the real genus field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt5)$. Thus the degree pattern $2^r,2^{r-1},2^{r-2}$ in the cyclic $2$-power hierarchy is a specialization of a uniform $C_{4M}$ theorem. We give exact low-class-number evaluations and certified computations at $D=-895,-3295,-8495$, separating respectively four, eight and sixteen non-genus Hecke $L(1)$-values and producing corresponding alternating Rogers-Ramanujan singular values. Classical mixed modular equations then give ordinary Rogers--Ramanujan companions at the same arguments.

title: A Multipatch Model for Evaluating Interdivisional Connectivity and Vaccination Dynamics in the 2026 Bangladesh Measles Outbreak
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18911v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The 2026 measles resurgence in Bangladesh motivates a spatial modelling framework that accounts for heterogeneous local transmission, vaccination activity, and interdivisional connectivity. We formulate a multipatch susceptible-vaccinated-infectious-recovered model for the eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. Division-specific parameters are estimated from reported measles cases \cite{DGHS} and smoothed vaccination data using bounded nonlinear least squares, with uncertainty quantified through 1000 parametric bootstrap replicates. The fitted divisional systems are then connected through compartment-specific movement and cross-patch infection coefficients adjusted for connectivity and the source division's relative reproduction number. The fitted model captures the main division-specific epidemic patterns. Estimated local reproduction numbers range from \(1.1386\) in Khulna (95\% CI:\(0.5703\)--\(1.3834\)) to \(4.3491\) in Dhaka (95\% CI: \(1.4449\)--\(5.6307\)), while Chattogram also exhibits high transmission potential (\(\mathcal{R}_0^i=4.2275\); 95\% CI: \(4.0019\)--\(4.3185\)). Baseline spatial coupling increases the network-wide epidemic peak from \(190.96\) to \(313.20\) infectious individuals and more than doubles cumulative infections from \(1086.42\) to \(2345.35\). Relative to baseline coupling, 50\% and 80\% restrictions reduce the epidemic peak by \(26.69\%\) and \(34.37\%\), and cumulative infections by \(25.07\%\) and \(41.48\%\), respectively. Conversely, a 50\% increase in spatial coupling raises the peak by \(30.14\%\) and cumulative infections by \(23.54\%\). Although local transmission remains dominant in every division, cross-patch infection accounts for \(28.83\%\) of new infections in Rajshahi at the baseline epidemic peak. Source-sink analysis identifies Dhaka as the dominant cross-patch source and Chattogram as a smaller secondary source.

title: There are only finitely many irregular Diophantine quadruples
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18912v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A set of $m$ distinct positive integers is called a Diophantine $m$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by one, is a perfect square. A Diophantine quadruple $\{a,b,c,d\}$ with $a<b><10^{338}$ and $d<10^{10^{24}}$.

title: A finite coefficient theory for shape identification in tilted generalized gamma families
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18915v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A continuous shape parameter enters both a radial density and the normalization of its transform coefficients. This coupling allows changes in shape to be compensated by changes in scale and exponential tilt. We study the coefficients b_k=e^a E[Y^k ]/[k!(d)_k ] for densities proportional to y^(d-1) exp(-{\alpha}y^q+\b{eta}y), with known integer q>=2, d,{\alpha}>0, and unrestricted real a,\b{eta}. For q=2, the first four coefficients determine all parameters globally, whereas three coefficients leave an analytic curve of solutions. We characterize the exact image of the two shape ratios and prove that two alternating corners decide whether an entire coefficient box is realizable and give its exact shape range. For every fixed q, the first q(q+1) coefficients give global identification and an everywhere full-rank map. A finite-difference criterion yields generic identification from 2q+1 coefficients, including every zero-tilt model against the full tilted family. For q=3, an exact rational certificate constructs two distinct shapes with identical first four coefficients and separated fifth coefficients. The results distinguish exact identification, realizability, and sensitivity for a parameter-dependent coefficient normalization.

title: Certifying non-existence of integer points on curves
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18916v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an elementary but powerful method for proving that a two-variable equation has no integer solutions. The method produces quadratic identities which every integer solution must satisfy. Once these identities are established, a standard quadratic reciprocity argument finishes the proof. We illustrate the power of the method by resolving $25$ out of $30$ two-variable equations of size up to $34$ for which the problem of integer solubility remained open. We also resolve the remaining $5$ equations by deeper methods, and further determine the integer solubility of all two-variable equations of size up to $35$ and of length up to $12$, with two exceptions. Before this work, there were $211$ equations in this category that resisted the previously known methods, and we proved that $209$ of them have no integer solutions, with all proofs formalized in Lean. In addition, we show that our method can be used to solve certain two-variable equations whose integer solution set is non-empty.

title: Short Proofs for the Minimum Number of Determined Circles
authors: Stijn Cambie, Denis Paliy, Rafa{\l} Wrona
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18918v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present short proofs for the main parts of the recently completed solution of Erd\H{o}s Problem 506, which asks for the minimum number of distinct circles determined by a finite planar point set that is neither collinear nor concyclic. An inversion argument and a seven-point line lemma show that eight points determine at least $17$ circles, and an explicit configuration attains this bound. A single argument combining Melchior's inequality with Langer's incidence bound establishes the sharp formula for every $n\ge15$. The proofs give concise alternatives to longer arguments in the recent literature; the remaining finite cases are cited separately.

title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18929v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$, $\theta\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}\mu$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $\mu$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and H\"{o}lder images. First, $\dim_{qH}\mu$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s><\dim_P\mu$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)<\dim_P\mu<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_P\mu_V=\min\{\dim_P\mu,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder maps $f_\omega:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $\mu$, $\dim_P\mu_{f_\omega}=m$ almost surely if and only if $\alpha m\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}\mu=\dim_P\mu$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.

title: On the Investigation of Antenna Beam Pattern Models for Fast Beam Placement in LEO Satellite Networks
authors: Ninh Thi-Thanh Tam, Nguyen Viet Anh, Nguyen Minh Quan, Trinh Van Chien
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18930v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the impact of antenna beam pattern models on the beam placement problem in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks. Unlike conventional beam placement studies that often rely on a fixed antenna pattern or a predefined half-power beamwidth, this work compares four representative gain models, namely the Bessel $J_1$ model, the combined Bessel $J_1+J_3$ model, the Gaussian model, and a 3GPP-TR 37.842 model. For each antenna pattern, the corresponding half-power angle is obtained and used to construct a user compatibility graph. The beam placement problem is then transformed into a Minimum Clique Cover problem and solved using a graph coloring-based algorithm. Numerical results compare the considered antenna models in terms of the number of active beams, load balancing, statistical channel gain-to-noise ratio (SCGNR), and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR). We analyze the impact of increasing the number of active beams on SINR-based spectral efficiency to explain the importance of carefully controlling the number of active beams. The results show that antenna beam pattern models affect both beam resource usage and link quality, highlighting the need for antenna-pattern-aware beam placement in LEO satellite networks.

title: From a Student's Question to the Half-Derivative: A Constructivist Teaching Model - Part I
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18932v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents a conceptual, cognitive-constructivist model for teaching the half-derivative. The model starts from a student's question and frames it as the problem of generalizing the familiar operation of differentiation. On a suitably chosen space of monomials, under the assumptions of linearity and of lowering the exponent by one half, the requirement that the operator applied twice give the ordinary derivative produces a recurrence for the coefficients. The freedom of normalization becomes visible, and an additional convention yields a formula compatible with the monomial rule of the Riemann-Liouville half-derivative. The domain of the operator and its relation to the Riemann-Liouville and Caputo operators are treated separately. The mathematical results rest on the author's earlier preprints; the contribution of this paper is their transformation into an instructional pathway organized in phases, with diagnostic questions, an analysis of typical errors, and comparative problems. The model is a design proposal: its effectiveness has not yet been established by systematic empirical research. The interactive Socratic implementation and the detailed diagnostics are the subject of Part II.

title: Generalized Pellet's theorem for analytic matrix-valued functions
authors: Hiromochi Itoh, Kei Matsushima, Takayuki Yamada
abstract:
arXiv:2610.18941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generalized Pellet's theorem is extended to analytic matrix-valued functions using Descartes' rule of signs for infinite series. Cauchy's estimate is incorporated to allow numerical computation of the bounds. To address the issue that Pellet's theorem and its generalizations may not always guarantee the existence of bounds, for the case of matrix size one, we employ the Dandelin- Lobachevsky-Graeffe method, which ensures the existence of the bounds for the roots and further improves them as the order of the transform increases. Without the need for any a priori information on the function, these theorems allow us to compute mathematically verified bounds for the roots in a certain region using an interval arithmetic implementation of the function. Numerical examples and an implementation are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Exponential Stability of Slow--Fast Stochastic Systems with a Small Delay
authors: Yudong Wang, Kele Sun, Shijie Zhou, Xuerong Mao
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the exponential stability of coupled slow--fast stochastic systems with a small delay. Under an averaged Lyapunov condition, we establish practical $p$th-moment exponential stability for $0

<2$ using a cutoff-function approach to handle singular Lyapunov derivatives near the origin. Exponential stability in the $p$th moment and almost surely is further obtained through two distinct mechanisms: homogeneous dissipation of the fast dynamics or vanishing sensitivity of the slow coefficients to the fast state near the origin. We extend these results to locally Lipschitz systems, establishing exponential stability with arbitrarily high probability for bounded sets of initial data, thereby broadening the applicability of stability analysis for stochastic systems with delayed feedback. Numerical examples illustrate our results.

title: A sharp discrete Sobolev inequality and left inverses of higher order differences
authors: Raul Hindov, Shahaf Nitzan, Jan-Fredrik Olsen, Eskil Rydhe
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19010v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For integers $\alpha,d \geqslant1$, we determine the best constants in the inequalities $||(a_j)_{j=1}^{d}||_{\ell^1} \leqslant C_{\alpha,d} ||((\Delta^\alpha a)_j)_{j=1}^{d+\alpha}||_{\ell^2},$ where $\Delta$ is the difference operator. We find that these constants correspond to the $\ell^2$ norm of the discrete Chebyshev polynomials, and show that the extremal sequences may be obtained by appropriate sampling of the discrete Landau polynomials. From beginning to end, this project was carried out without use of AI.

title: Mixing Rates for Analytic Observables: Toral Endomorphisms and Anosov Blaschke Deformations
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19019v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze exponential mixing for analytic observables and show that mixing at a double exponential rate occurs for genuinely nonlinear systems. Neither its presence nor its sharp exponent is stable under arbitrarily small area-preserving perturbations in the real-analytic topology.
  We construct two families of area-preserving Anosov Blaschke product diffeomorphisms that converge in the real-analytic topology to the same hyperbolic toral automorphism. For nonzero parameters, both deformations are topologically conjugate to the linear model but not $C^1$-conjugate. For all nonzero parameter values, the maps in the first family are mixing at a double exponential rate with the same sharp exponent, strictly smaller than that of the linear map. The sharp exponent is therefore not lower semicontinuous at the linear map. In the second family, mixing at a double exponential rate is lost altogether, although the maps remain exponentially mixing.
  We also establish double exponential bounds for every ergodic toral endomorphism and uniform bounds of the same type for totally ergodic higher-rank toral actions. Our method combines the Fourier escape argument with Koopman operator estimates from a Hilbert space of analytic functions to its dual space of hyperfunctions.

title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs
authors: Justin Dumouchelle, Shunyu Yao, Beste Basciftci, Thiago Serra
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Chance-constrained stochastic programs (CCSPs) require solutions that satisfy uncertain constraints with high probability. Standard approaches either embed scenarios directly into optimization by considering sample average approximation (SAA)-based reformulations, growing prohibitively expensive and often failing to find feasible solutions; or employ conservative reformulations that guarantee feasibility but sacrifice objective quality by design. We propose ACCESS (Adaptive Chance-Constrained Exploration via Structured Sampling), a structured sampling framework that decouples optimization from feasibility evaluation. First, high-quality candidate solutions are generated by solving many inexpensive single-scenario subproblems, avoiding sampling directly in the constrained high-dimensional solution space. Second, feasibility is assessed separately via large-scale batched simulation over a massive number of scenarios, which is naturally amenable to GPU parallelism. That reduces the search from a high-dimensional solution space to a two-dimensional parameter space controlling conservatism and scenario diversity; while concentrating on candidates near the feasibility boundary, where high-quality feasible solutions lie. We also introduce a variant, ACCESS($\delta$), which provides certified feasibility guarantees with probability $1-\delta$. Experiments across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions show that ACCESS matches or exceeds the best objective found by any method in nearly every setting, while ACCESS($\delta$) is empirically feasible on every instance. The conservative reformulations remain several percent worse in objective, and SAA is frequently infeasible while taking an order of magnitude longer on the harder benchmarks.

title: First-order Optimization Methods with Generalized Smoothness for Low-rank Matrix Factorization
authors: A. V. Bidanets, F. S. Stonyakin
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19059v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies several first-order methods for low-rank matrix minimization in the Burer--Monteiro form, where the target matrix is represented as the product of a nonnegative factor matrix and its transpose. Such a factorization destroys convexity of the objective function and global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient. We prove that for a quadratic objective function that is strongly convex only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, the Burer-Monteiro factorized objective possesses generalized smoothness with a fractional exponent 2/3. For a quadratic objective, the generalized smoothness property requires positive definiteness of the operator A only on the subspace of symmetric matrices, which relaxes the assumptions of Dragomir et al. On this basis, three methods are proposed: an adaptive gradient descent method with Armijo backtracking; an unconstrained SafeAdam method combining the Adam direction with a descent-angle certificate and a fallback to the normalized gradient; and a certified projected version for the nonnegativity constraint. Global convergence and explicit convergence rates for the proposed methods have been proved. The obtained convergence rate is better than the convergence rate of ordinary unaccelerated gradient descent in the case of a sufficiently large gradient. In the small-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of square-root type, and the corresponding complexity scales as the inverse square of the desired accuracy. In the large-gradient regime, the convergence guarantee is of three-quarters type, and the corresponding complexity is proportional to the inverse of the accuracy raised to the power of 4/3. Experiments on SymNMF using the TDT2, Reuters and CBCL datasets, which are standard benchmarks for document and image clustering, show that the methods match or outperform Dyn-NoLips without tuning the relative-smoothness kernel parameters.

title: Neural Spline Flow Diffeomorphisms for Pullback Finite Element Methods on Complex Domains
authors: Ioannis Kalogeris, Anaksagoras Spitas, Konstantinos Atzarakis, George Stavroulakis, Vissarion Papadopoulos
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19092v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a method for solving partial differential equations on complex domains by learning smooth, invertible mappings from a fixed reference domain using Neural Spline Flows (NSFs). Monotone rational-quadratic spline coupling layers ensure a strictly positive Jacobian determinant by construction, eliminating the need for Jacobian-sign penalties. A diffeomorphic pullback transfers the weak form of the PDE to the reference domain, enabling finite element analysis on reusable structured meshes. To generalize across shapes, a shared NSF is conditioned on low-dimensional latent codes learned through an auto-decoder framework; a subsequent encoder predicts these codes for unseen geometries in a single forward pass. For a given learned map, the pullback preserves the mathematical structure of the PDE and is exactly equivalent to solving on the domain represented by that map. Because the learned domain generally approximates the target geometry, geometric mapping error remains distinct from finite element discretization and quadrature errors. Numerical benchmarks show that sufficiently accurate learned mappings yield reliable finite element solutions. By avoiding repeated generation of unstructured meshes, the method addresses a bottleneck in simulation workflows. The fixed reference mesh also creates opportunities for efficient assembly, memory-aligned data access, and precomputed quadrature. The resulting framework assigns geometric complexity to the neural network while retaining conventional finite element discretization and convergence properties on the learned domain, with overall accuracy also governed by geometric fidelity.

title: $L^p_\mu$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19151v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_\mu$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $\mu$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $\gamma$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.

title: Even and Odd Integer Values of the Secondary Zeta Function
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19175v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The secondary zeta function is defined by $$ Z(s)=\sum_{\gamma>0}\frac{1}{\gamma^{s}}, $$ where $\tfrac12+i\gamma$ runs over the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function with positive ordinate, and the Riemann hypothesis is assumed throughout. In this article, we derive convergent integral representations of $Z(s)$ at positive even and odd integer argument, expressed through a differential operator acting on the logarithm of the Riemann $\xi$-function. Define $$ L(x)=\log\left(\frac{\xi(x+\tfrac12)}{\xi(\tfrac12)}\right), \qquad \mathcal{E}=x\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}, \qquad \mathcal{D}_k=\mathcal{E}\prod_{j=1}^{k}(\mathcal{E}-2j). $$ Then, for $k\geq1$, $$ Z(2k)=\frac{(-1)^k}{2^k(k-1)!}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\mathcal{D}_k L(x)}{x^{2k+1}}\,\mathrm{d}x $$ and $$ Z(2k+1)=\frac{(-1)^k}{\pi\,(2k-1)!!}\int_{0}^{\infty}\frac{\mathcal{D}_k L(x)}{x^{2k+2}}\,\mathrm{d}x. $$ In the last part, we write these formulas out explicitly for $Z(k)$, $2\leq k\leq 7$, both in terms of $L(x)$ and in terms of $\xi(x+\tfrac12)$ for reference. We also derive a limit formula for $\gamma_1$, the ordinate of the first nontrivial zero, and demonstrate its convergence numerically.

title: Aggregated Column Generation for Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
authors: Harshit Kothari, James Luedtke, Luke Marshall
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19181v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation applied to two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs (SMIP) has been shown empirically to yield a formulation with strong bounds that can be solved via column generation. However, the time to solve the restricted master problem grows significantly with the number of scenarios due to the increasing number of nonanticipativity constraints (NACs). Moreover, the associated high-dimensional dual space can cause the dual multipliers to oscillate between iterations, further slowing convergence. We propose an aggregated column generation framework for solving a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation. Applied to SMIP, this method partitions the NACs into groups and replaces each group with a weighted surrogate constraint, leading to a reduced size and providing implicit stabilization by restricting the dual space. While aggregation leads to a relaxation, we develop two strategies for recovering the standard Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation bound. The first iteratively refines the partition by splitting groups that contain violated constraints. The second keeps the partition fixed and adaptively updates the aggregation weights. We prove convergence of the two approaches and study their computational performance on two benchmark problem classes.

title: Finite-sample certification of coverage regret for budgeted document selection under adaptive stratified auditing
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19207v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Selecting a budget-constrained set of documentary fragments, for instance the knowledge base of a retrieval-augmented generation system, raises a statistical question: how much expected query coverage is lost relative to the best feasible selection when the query distribution is unknown? We construct finite-sample, distribution-free upper confidence bounds for this coverage regret that remain valid after data-dependent selection. A pilot stage may select the document set, screen competitors, build comparison networks and learn an annotation policy. Then an independent audit acquires relevance labels with probabilities that are constant within observable strata. The main result is a simultaneous bound for all retained coverage contrasts. The bound is made observable by empirical-Bernstein variance calibration or by a one-stage construction without calibration, and it accounts for estimated stratum proportions. For maximum-type coverage we prove variance contractions for swaps of redundant fragments, give a condition under which multiscale radii improve on a direct union bound, and show that such redundancy cannot be certified from samples alone. A simulation study confirms validity and quantifies the gains from variance calibration and certified redundancy.

title: Pointwise minimax lower bounds under a multi-index constraint: the price of an unknown orientation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19208v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider nonparametric regression with random design and non-Gaussian noise, where the regression function has the multi-index form $F(x)=f(\Theta x)$ with an unknown link $f:\RR^m\to\RR$ in an anisotropic H\"older class and an unknown matrix $\Theta$ with $m\le d$ orthonormal rows. For estimation of $F$ at a fixed point we prove that the minimax risk is bounded from below by a multiple of $L^{1/(2\gamma+1)}(n^{-1}\ln n)^{\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}$, where $\gamma$ is the harmonic mean of the smoothness indices of the link divided by $m$. For $m<d$ this extends a Gaussian white noise result to regression. The main new case is $m=d$, where no dimension reduction takes place: the logarithmic factor still appears as soon as the link is anisotropic and the orientation of its axes is unknown. In contrast, when the link is isotropic with smoothness index at most one, the class is rotation invariant up to a constant and the classical rate without logarithm is attained. The logarithmic loss is therefore caused by the unknown orientation of the directions in which the function is least smooth

title: The grounded spirituality of mathematics
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19216v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose that mathematics is done largely as a means of both coping with and celebrating our physicality in the natural world. Inspired by David Abram's "Becoming Animal", we suggest that -- in opposition to the popular image of an otherworldy Platonic realm-- the spiritual component of doing mathematics is grounded on and in the Earth. We explore this as a means of questioning the widespread adoption of AI in the workflows of research mathematics.

title: An oral history of FPSAC
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As its 40th anniversary nears, we present a history of the International Conference on Formal Power Series and Algebraic Combinatorics (FPSAC), through interviews with figures from its past, present, and future.

title: Natural Geometry Based on the Rectilinear Plane
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19253v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The aim of this note is to introduce natural geometry, in which the rectilinear plane is a primitive. This plane is admitted together with its rectitude, and its rectitude states that a Lambert quadrilateral has its fourth angle right. The fourth angle of a Lambert quadrilateral may be right, acute or obtuse, and this trichotomy distinguishes three planes. Starting from the rectitude, we prove the uniqueness of the parallel by a chain of neutral steps: the rectangle, the triangle whose angles sum to $\pi$, and Legendre's theorem \cite{legendre}, all borrowed from the classical literature. That uniqueness is equivalent to the fifth postulate, which we thus reach in Euclid's own wording: the equivalence is read in the natural direction, and it is not a derivation of the fifth postulate from the other four, since the independence of that postulate is not in question. In the rectilinear plane the parallels are characterised as exactly the images of a line under a point-reflection, and equivalently as the pairs of equidistant lines. The other two planes are then placed beside the rectilinear one, and the same definitions serve for all three.

title: Variationally correct loss functions for nonlinear parametric problems and their neural approximations
authors: Pablo Cort\'es Castillo, Wolfgang Dahmen, Jay Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19296v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We construct computable a posteriori error estimators for parametric families of nonlinear elliptic problems by measuring the residual of a variational formulation in the dual norm of a closed subspace of the test space. A single abstract theorem shows that the resulting estimator is bounded above and below by the error in the trial norm, i.e., it is a variationally correct loss function. Two instances are covered. The first considers an $L_2$-like test space, yielding a nonlinear first-order system least-squares loss function that certifies arbitrary, possibly meshless, approximations. The second breaks the test space, yielding a nonlinear discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin loss function computed by element-local problems. All assumptions are verified for quasilinear diffusion, including monotone fluxes and semilinear problems, and a nonlocal Kirchhoff model. Numerical studies train neural networks approximating the parameter-to-solution maps with the latter loss and measure the ratio of loss to squared error.

title: The Capacity of the Noisy Torn Paper Channel and the Noisy Shuffling Channel
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19300v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The torn paper channel breaks a codeword into fragments and returns all fragments without their original order. The noisy torn paper channel additionally introduces bit substitution errors to each fragment. Recovering the message therefore requires accounting for both bit errors and uncertainty about the fragment order. We establish a capacity upper bound for the noisy torn paper channel that matches the achievable rate of Ravi, Vahid, and Shomorony and resolves their conjecture. Our results also determine the capacity of the noisy shuffling channel of Shomorony and Heckel, in which all fragments have the same length, and resolve their open question.

title: Solving a sequence of eigenvalue problems using snapshot and row subsampling
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19326v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A sequence of eigenvalue problems requires solving $A_i\vec{x}_i= \lambda_i\vec{x}_i$ where $i \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $N \gg 1$ and (usually) $\lambda_i$ is the largest or smallest eigenvalue of $A_i$. Often, the matrices $A_i$ come from a discretization of a smooth map depending on a parameter $p \rightarrow A(p)$, that is $A_i = A(p_i)$, so the matrices $A_i$ change gradually along the sequence. Under this latter assumption, we introduce an efficient algorithm for solving sequences of eigenvalue problems. Our algorithm combines the ideas of reduced order model and row subsampling, as done in [E. Jones and Y. Nakatsukasa, arXiv, 2025] for linear systems. In addition, in our approach, the same set of rows is guaranteed to work well independently of the value of the parameter $p$ or the matrix $A(p)$ as long as the snapshot matrix is unchanged and given that the row subset was chosen well at the beginning. Furthermore, we implement an update strategy of the snapshot matrix. Along these results, we present theoretical analysis of the snapshot matrix for eigenvalue problems, showing an exponential decay of the singular values, and we give bounds on the error on eigenvectors for unseen value of the parameter. This analysis generalizes that in [M. Guido, D. Kressner, and P. Ricci, J. Sci. Comput., 2024] and shows that, regardless of the distribution of the snapshot points, the convergence is always (asymptotically) exponential in the number of snapshot points if the function $A(p)$ admits an analytical extension. We further generalize our algorithm for computing largest or smallest singular values and relative singular vectors and to generalized eigenvalue problems. We conclude with numerical results showing the efficiency of our approach.

title: Uniqueness of Limit Cycles for Abel Equations and Planar Systems
authors: Jos\'e Luis Bravo Trinidad, Renhao Tian, Yulin Zhao
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19340v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study positive limit cycles of the Abel equation $$\dot{x}=A(t)x^{3}+B(t)x^{2},$$ where $A$ and $B$ are $2\pi$-periodic functions. By developing a half-period convexity method, we establish a new criterion ensuring that the equation has at most one positive limit cycle. Moreover, if such a limit cycle exists, it is hyperbolic. As applications, we consider two classes of planar polynomial systems that can be reduced to Abel equations. For a subfamily of cubic rigid systems, we prove that there is at most one limit cycle, thereby giving a partial answer to the first problem in Gasull's list of 33 open problems. For quadratic systems, we derive a new uniqueness criterion for limit cycles surrounding the origin and provide explicit parameter regions under which the criterion is satisfied.

title: On Local Inference for Functionals of Ill-Posed Inverse Problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19350v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study inference for continuous linear functionals of solutions to ill-posed inverse problems, including Euclidean parameters arising in nonparametric instrumental variables, proximal causal inference, and shadow-variable models. Although pointwise root-$n$ inference is possible under standard conditions, we show that this need not translate into locally reliable inference. Under a model imposing only minimal regularity conditions, the target is Hellinger discontinuous when both inverse problems are ill-posed: arbitrarily small changes in the data-generating law can produce arbitrarily large changes in the target, ruling out informative locally uniform inference. Imposing a uniform bound on a minimum-norm solution restores Hellinger continuity under regularity conditions, but does not by itself ensure stable root-n inference. If, in addition, both inverse problems are ill-posed and the solution whose norm is uniformly bounded is nonunique at a law $P_0$, then under regularity conditions the target fails to be pathwise differentiable; consequently, asymptotically linear estimators exhibit nonvanishing root-$n$ bias under some local alternatives, causing Wald confidence intervals to undercover asymptotically. Under regularity conditions, pathwise differentiability is restored if the uniformly bounded solution is unique at $P_0$. It is also restored, regardless of uniqueness, under the stronger requirement that the corresponding solution satisfy a uniformly bounded $\beta$-source condition for some $\beta$>0. We relate these regimes to very weak, weak, and strong identification in instrumental variables models.

title: Discrete Edge Multiscale Space based Hybrid Schwarz Preconditioner for High-Frequency Helmholtz Problems
authors: Shubin Fu, Shihua Gong, Guanglian Li, Yueqi Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19354v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this work, we develop a novel hybrid Schwarz method, termed as edge multiscale space based hybrid Schwarz (EMs-HS), for solving the Helmholtz problem with large wavenumbers. The problem is discretized using $H^1$-conforming nodal finite element methods on meshes of size $h$ decreasing faster than $k^{-3/2}$ such that the discretization error can be bounded by the data uniformly with respect to $k$. EMs-HS consists of a one-level Schwarz preconditioner (RAS-imp) and a coarse solver in a multiplicative way. The RAS-imp preconditioner solves local problems on overlapping subdomains with impedance boundary conditions in parallel, and combines the local solutions using partition of unity. On the PDE level, this coarse space corresponds to an edge multiscale space proposed in {[S. Fu, G. Li, R. Craster, and S. Guenneau, \emph{Multiscale Model. Simul.}, 19(4):1684-1709, 2021]}. The approximation properties of this coarse space to the discrete solutions from the primal and adjoint problems are derived by a novel conforming Galerkin finite element method based upon a nonstandard variational formulation. This work represents the first theoretical analysis of an edge multiscale space at the discrete level. We prove that the EMs-HS preconditioner leads to a convergent fixed-point iteration uniformly for large wavenumbers, by rigorously analyzing the approximation properties of the coarse space to the global Helmholtz harmonic extension part and to the solution of the adjoint problem. We provide extensive numerical results on the sharpness of the theoretical findings and also demonstrate the method on challenging heterogeneous models.

title: Poincar\'e compactifications of pullbacks of parallel vector fields under counterexamples to the real Jacobian conjecture
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19360v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $F: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polynomial map with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant. It is known that the global invertibility of $F$ is equivalent to the pullback of a parallel vector field being parallel. In this paper, we construct the phase portraits on the Poincar\'e disc of the pullbacks of the canonical annular, radial, and strip vector fields under non-injective maps $F$ that have recently appeared in the literature. Our arguments use local and global properties of vector fields as well as local and global properties of functions, thereby connecting techniques from dynamical systems and singularity theory.

title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19409v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.

title: Softplus Affine(1, 1) Processes: Enlarged Stationarity Region, Stationary Unit Roots, and Inference
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19421v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Softplus affine\((1,1)\) models keep the conditional mean positive while allowing coefficients of either sign. We study them under Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related conditional distributions. A stationary solution with moments of all positive orders exists whenever the coefficient sum is less than one, strictly enlarging previously known sufficient regions. At the unit root, the coefficient sum equals one. Under an invertibility condition, a stationary solution exists in this case if and only if the intercept is negative. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail with an explicit index, and the observations can exhibit long memory. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal at the usual \(\sqrt n\) rate below and at the unit root, with the coefficient sum left unrestricted in estimation. At the unit root, these results require only a finite mean and yield standard Wald inference even when the observations have infinite variance or long memory. Simulations and two applications examine finite-sample inference and sensitivity to the softplus scale.

title: A potential projection method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with low regularity potential
authors: Weizhu Bao, Qingyuan Sun, Chushan Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a potential projection (PP) method for the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation (NLSE) with low-regularity and singular potentials by replacing the potential with its Fourier projection (truncated Fourier series). This gives rise to an NLSE with projected potential (NLSEwPP). We rigorously establish its well-posedness under low-regularity potentials, and its convergence to the original NLSE. The NLSEwPP is then directly discretized by the standard time-splitting Fourier pseudospectral (TS-FP) method with the mesh size chosen according to the potential projection parameter, resulting in the fully discrete TS-PP-FP method. Numerically, TS-PP-FP consistently achieves optimal temporal and spatial convergence rates with respect to the regularity of the exact solution under low-regularity and even singular potentials. Compared with the time-splitting Fourier spectral method, TS-PP-FP attains the same convergence rates at significantly lower computational cost and preserves the mass conservation and time symmetry (that are lost in the Fourier spectral discretization of the time-splitting method); compared with the time-splitting FP method, it is substantially more accurate for low-regularity potentials with the same computational cost.

title: A pure source transfer domain decomposition method for Helmholtz equations in 3D unbounded domain
authors: Xinran Bai, Yu Du, Haijun Wu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19435v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop and analyze a three-dimensional pure source transfer domain decomposition method (PSTDDM) for the Helmholtz equation in free space. Extending the two-dimensional PSTDDM proposed by [Du and Wu, J. Sci. Comput., 83(2020),83:68], the proposed method transfers sources successively along the $x_1$, $x_2$, and $x_3$ directions, yielding layer-wise, bar-wise, and block-wise PSTDDMs. The main challenge in the convergence analysis is deriving wavenumber-explicit truncation-error estimates. To address this challenge, we establish inf--sup conditions for the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem under relaxed restrictions on the PML parameters and reformulate the source-transfer operators. We then introduce a positive-definite reconstruction step that produces a globally conforming approximation. In addition, a new quantitative lower bound is established for the imaginary part of the complex PML distance, more easily yielding exponential decay estimates in three dimensions. These lead to wavenumber-explicit convergence estimates for all three PSTDDMs. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods both as direct solvers and as preconditioners for GMRES.

title: Large-Step Last-Iterate Convergence of Random-Reshuffling Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19444v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Random reshuffling stochastic gradient descent (RR-SGD) is widely used for finite-sum optimization in machine learning. For convex $L$-smooth components, recent work establishes convergence guarantees for an averaged iterate with component stepsizes as large as order $1/L$. However, the final iterate is a natural output in practice, and existing last-iterate guarantees in this setting require stepsizes that scale inversely with the number of components $n$. We establish an expected objective-gap bound for the last iterate of standard RR-SGD on unconstrained problems with a constant component stepsize satisfying $0<\eta\lesssim 1/(L(1 + \log(nK)))$, where $K$ is the number of epochs. By retaining the sampling bias at random comparison points, we remove the explicit $1/n$ factor from the stepsize restriction. Combined with existing small-step bounds, our result matches the corresponding averaged-iterate convergence rate up to logarithmic factors.

title: High-Girth QLDPC Codes from Circulant and Affine Permutation Matrices
authors: Vahid Nourozi, Roxana Smarandache, David G. M. Mitchell{\dag}
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19451v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study two explicit constructions of binary Calderbank--Shor--Steane quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes with check weight six. The first uses a fixed circulant shift pattern and yields parameters $\code{6N}{2N+2}{6}$ with Tanner graph girth twelve for $N=31$ and every $N\ge37$. A graph incidence interpretation gives the ranks and girths, and a uniform weight six logical operator establishes the exact distance. The second construction uses fixed matrix polynomials with circulant and affine permutation coefficients. Here, a polynomial commutation identity guarantees orthogonality for every cyclic lift. Four realizations give $[[192,16,8]]$, $[[288,16,12]]$, $[[384,16,14]]$, and $[[576,32,20]]$, with Tanner girth eight and computationally certified distances. We give reproducible construction data, distinguish classical cycle distance from quantum distance, and identify the limitations of both families.

title: Weak Private Information Retrieval for Graph-based Storage under $\epsilon$-privacy
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19456v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The problem of Private Information Retrieval (PIR) across graph-based replicated systems has seen a surge of interest in recent literature. In such systems, servers are modeled as the vertices of a graph, and each file is represented by an edge connecting the pair of servers that store it. While previous research on Graph-PIR (G-PIR) has focused mostly on perfect information-theoretic privacy, relaxing this constraint has the potential for significantly higher retrieval rates. In this work, we consider the setting of Graph-based Weak Private Information Retrieval (G-WPIR), under an $\epsilon$-privacy metric. We adapt an existing G-WPIR scheme for arbitrary graphs to analyze its performance under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the expected download cost for arbitrary graphs under the $\epsilon$-privacy metric and derive from it an explicit rate upper bound for complete graphs. Finally, we show the achievable rate-privacy trade-offs for two specific graph classes---complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs.

title: Convergence Rates of Factorized Gradient Descent for Overparameterized Asymmetric Matrix Sensing with Balancing Regularization
authors: Yongjun Chen, Jiaming Zhang, Liping Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19477v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study factorized gradient descent (FGD) for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with the balancing regularizer $\frac18\|L^\top L-R^\top R\|_F^2$. An exact indefinite lifting of the population objective decomposes the dynamics of FGD into positive, negative, and null spectral subspaces. The first two components have linear restoring terms, whereas the null component contracts only quadratically. For independent isotropic sub-Gaussian sensing matrices and independent centered sub-Gaussian noise with scale proxy $\sigma$, we prove the local bound \[
  \|L_tR_t^\top-X^\star\|_2
  \lesssim\max\left\{\frac{1}{\eta t+1/\sigma_r},
  \kappa\sigma\sqrt{\frac{d_1+d_2}{n}}\right\}, \] under a sufficiently small initialization error, the number of linear measurements $n\gtrsim\kappa^2(d_1+d_2)\max\{k^2,\sigma^2/\sigma_r^2\}$, and step size $\eta\lesssim\sigma_1^{-1}$. Here $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_r$ are the largest and smallest nonzero singular values of the target $X^\star\in \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times d_2}$ respectively, and $\kappa=\sigma_1/\sigma_r$. Furthermore, a population trajectory was constructed to have tight product error $\Theta(1/t)$. These results provide a local rate characterization for ordinary gradient descent for overparameterized asymmetric matrix sensing with balancing regularizer.

title: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation for In-Band Full-Duplex Systems Based on Transformer Neural Operators
authors: Zhijie Su, Shiquan Zhang, Qiaolin He
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19490v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Digital-domain self-interference cancellation is essential in in-band full-duplex radios after passive suppression and analog cancellation. It is particularly challenging when the desired signal is strong relative to the residual self-interference. In this regime, conventional iterative digital cancellers update their coefficients from desired-signal-contaminated received samples and may suffer substantial performance degradation. This paper reformulates digital-domain self-interference cancellation as an operator-learning problem. The proposed framework learns the temporal evolution of the residual self-interference channel from historical observations and uses the learned operator together with the known local transmit signal to reconstruct the current residual self-interference. A Transformer neural operator is used to realize this framework. The resulting method is trained in a desired-signal-free setting and then applied in the presence of a desired signal. A continuity-based analysis characterizes the sensitivity of the learned operator to the resulting input perturbation. Numerical experiments in static and time-varying channels, including time-varying SIR conditions, demonstrate stable cancellation performance over a wide range of interference levels. At 30 dB SIR, the proposed method improves the cancellation performance by 5--15 dB over the considered conventional methods.

title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part I
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19501v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the circle-relation subspace $O_n^\circ(V)$ in the defining relations of the level-$n$ Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. We assemble the residue relations generating $O_n^\circ(V)$ into generating functions and obtain an explicit recursion that replaces every sufficiently deep mode by retained modes with indices at least $-2n-1$, modulo $O_n^\circ(V)$. This recursion is encoded in a left truncated field $Y_L$. Since such mode replacements are valid only in the leftmost position of an operator product, we prove the replacement, derivative, commutator, and one-step iterate identities for $Y_L$ needed for finite-length calculations.
  For a finite homogeneous strong generating set $S$, we define the finite-length circle subspaces $O_n^\circ(N,S,V)$ and their plus subspaces. We formulate a finite-length conjecture under an explicit auxiliary-degree hypothesis and a separate termwise conjecture for the correction residues of one-sided iterates. We prove reductions to the $k=0$ strip and to last vacuum mode $-1$, recover the length-one relation spaces, and give explicit Virasoro computations at word length two for $n=1$ and $n=2$. The $Y_L$ identities are the input for the companion paper (Part II).

title: Right Coideal Subalgebras, Hopf Galois Objects, and $\imath$-Hopf Algebras
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19503v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study right comodule algebras and their connections with Hopf bi-Galois objects and right coideal subalgebras. For a Hopf $2$-cocycle $\sigma$ on $K$ and a unital right-colinear algebra map $\Gamma:A\to K$, we show that $\Gamma:A_\sigma\to K^\sigma$ is an algebra map precisely when $\sigma$ is trivial on $\operatorname{im}\Gamma\otimes\operatorname{im}\Gamma$. We describe comodule-algebra morphisms $A_\sigma\to K^\sigma$ by characters and establish injectivity criteria using the coradical and extensions of characters to convolution-invertible functionals. For coactions on Hopf quotients projecting to the coproduct, character-evaluation maps are injective, and equality of their images is determined by a unique algebra character.
  For the $\imath$-Hopf algebras $H^\imath_\tau$ of Chen--Lu--Pan--Ruan--Wang, with $H$ having a bijective antipode and a Hopf pairing, we obtain a Hopf bi-Galois realization $H^\imath_\tau\hookrightarrow F_\sigma(H\otimes H^{\mathrm{cop}})$. We identify algebra characters with nonzero $\tau$-twisted compatible maps $\chi$ and prove that the corresponding morphisms $\xi_{\tau,\chi}$ of Chen--Lu--Pan--Ruan--Wang are injective, yielding right coideal realizations in $(H\otimes H)^\imath$. We classify the $H^\imath_\tau$ up to comodule-algebra isomorphism and determine when these realizations have the same image.

title: A Stabilized CR-CR Method for Fourth-Order Elliptic Problems
authors: Yule Sun, Shudan Tian, Qian Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.19514v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a CR-CR method for strain gradient elasticity and prove its robustness with respect to the Lame parameter $\lambda$ and the length scale $\iota$. The method introduces the strain as an independent symmetric tensor and discretizes both the strain and the displacement using CR elements. The commuting properties of the CR interpolation operator with the relevant differential operators leads the robustness with respect to $\lambda$. A stabilization term weakly imposes the relation between the strain and the symmetric gradient of the displacement. The method also applies directly to the biharmonic equation and singularly perturbed fourth-order problems. For these problems, we prove that the CR-CR method is equivalent to an RT-CR method proposed by Huang and Tang. This result extends the classical equivalence between the RT-P0 mixed method and the CR method for the Poisson equation to fourth-order problems. The equivalence shows that the stabilization term arises naturally from the RT-CR mixed formulation.
